summary: Isabelle Ratié is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Paris 1, the EPHE under Lyne Bansat-Boudon, and under Alexis Sanderson. She held posts at Leipzig, Sorbonne Nouvelle (2014–2025), and was appointed professor at the Collège de France in 2025.

Isaiah Berlin was a philosopher and historian who studied at St Paul's School and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1928–1932). He held an academic post at the University of Oxford from around 1932 to 1975.

Isaline Blew Horner was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Newnham College and Cambridge under Caroline Rhys Davids. She held positions at Newnham College, Cambridge, and served as Honorary Secretary of the Pali Text Society.
Isamu Kanaji was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who was a professor at Shitennoji University and International Buddhist University Junior College (both attested 1976).

Isao Nishitani is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He was affiliated with Sennyu-ji (attested 2016) and served as an associate professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (attested 2026).

Iselin Frydenlund works in Buddhist and religious studies. She held posts as a senior researcher at the Peace Research Institute Oslo and as a research fellow at the University of Oslo (both attested 2016).

Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was an Indologist and philosopher educated at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Sanskrit College. He taught and worked at Fort William College, Sanskrit College, and served as Direktor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in 1851.

Iso Kern works in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at KU Leuven, Freiburg, Heidelberg, and National Taiwan University, he worked at the Husserl Archives, taught at Heidelberg, Zurich, and Fribourg, and became Titularprofessor at Bern in 1985.
Issaien Ikeyama was a scholar in Buddhist studies who held professorial posts at Eizan Gakuin and International Buddhist University Junior College (attested 1976).
Issei Suzuki was a Buddhist studies scholar who was educated at Rissho University and later served as a professor there.
Issei Yamakawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed studies at Sophia University and earned a master's degree at Aichi Gakuin University.

Itsuko Nishikawa is a scholar of linguistics and Japanese studies. She studied at Teachers College, Columbia University, and served as a Teaching Professor at the University of Washington (attested 2026).
Itsuo Asako is a Japanese studies and Buddhist studies scholar who served at Hanazono University as an associate professor (attested 1997) and professor emeritus (attested 2026).

Ivan Minayev was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1858–1862) and held a post in its Faculty of Oriental Studies from around 1871 to 1890.

Ivan Pavlovich Minaev was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University and under Albrecht Weber and Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev. He later served as a professor at Saint Petersburg State University.

Ives Goddard is a linguist who was educated at Harvard College and Harvard University (~1959–1969). He held posts at Harvard University (~1969–1975), the Smithsonian Institution (~1975–2021), and the National Museum of Natural History (~1975–2021).
Ives Waldo is a scholar of philosophy, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Oxford and studied under traditional teacher Chögyam Trungpa from 1970 to 1988.

Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Harvard University (-2003), studying under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, Charles Hallisey, and Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and held a fellowship at Grinnell College.
Ivo Fišer was an Indologist who served as a lecturer at Charles University (attested 1960) and held a post in the Institute for Indian Philology at the University of Copenhagen (attested 1970).

Iwao Ishikawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He held research and lecturing posts at Toho Kenkyukai, the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
